labels.chartVerifyTitle: How this app checks its calculations
labels.chartVerifySummary: Every time the app changes, tests compare its solar-term times and four pillars with separate calculations. This checks that the calculation is right; it doesn't mean the readings come true.
labels.chartVerify.0.title: Solar terms (1900–2100)
labels.chartVerify.0.body: The app holds the start times of 2,412 solar terms, computed from NASA JPL's DE440s ephemeris. Against a separate astronomical calculation they differ by 0.25 seconds on average and 0.53 seconds at most.
labels.chartVerify.1.title: Four pillars
labels.chartVerify.1.body: Tests compare them with two other calculation libraries: 5,000 randomly chosen births (lunar-python) and 2,000 births in Korea (manseryeok-js). Cases where a library follows a different rule (within minutes of a solar term, how the zi hour is split, and so on) are marked and left out of that comparison.
labels.chartVerify.2.title: Seoul and other cities
labels.chartVerify.2.body: 1,850 births in Seoul and 8 other cities, each calculated with both zi-hour rules and with longitude correction on and off (7,400 charts), all matched the astronomical calculation (October 2026).
labels.chartVerify.3.title: Daylight saving and standard time
labels.chartVerify.3.body: Daylight saving and standard time come from the time-zone records (IANA time zone data) for that place and date. The result is shown above under “Time used”.
labels.chartVerify.4.title: Same chart, same words
labels.chartVerify.4.body: The same person, day and settings always give the same reading. Nothing is picked at random.

labels.why.rule.day: How the day's certainty is set: from the day's stem, the day's branch and any clash or pairing with your day branch. If any of them points against the day's side, it is conditional. With none against and two or more pointing the same way as the day, it is firm. Otherwise it is a tendency.
labels.why.rule.luck: How this certainty is set: from the bases of the luck's grade. If any basis points against the grade, it is conditional. With none against and two or more on the same side as the grade, it is firm. Otherwise it is a tendency. For an even grade, it is conditional when bases point both ways and a tendency otherwise. A year's flow also counts that year's ten-year luck as one basis when it is high or low. When your strength sits near the cutoff it is never firm, and without a birth time, a judgment that changes with the hour is never firm.
labels.why.rule.question: How a question's certainty is set, in this order: a quiet answer, where the energy asked about doesn't show up at that time, is a tendency. If the luck of that time, or a helping character, points against the answer, it is conditional. Otherwise, two or more bases on the same side as the answer make it firm, and anything else is a tendency. An answer that changes with the birth hour is never firm.
labels.why.rule.report: How a report's certainty is set: each kind of paragraph has its own set certainty. Kinds chosen only when different bases agree are firm, kinds chosen from one basis are tendencies, and kinds that join opposite bases or split the cases are conditional. Paragraphs about a luck grade follow that luck's certainty. The same characters counted in two ways count once.
labels.why.rule.yearPart: How this certainty is set: the theme, the areas and the year's second note are firm only when the year's flow is firm and that character points the same way as the year's grade. Otherwise they are tendencies. So they can be firm with a single basis listed. If the side changes with the birth hour, they are never firm.
labels.why.rule.decade: How the ten-year line is set: from the grades of your ten-year luck and of this year's own energy. Same side: firm. Opposite sides: conditional. This year's energy even: a tendency. When the ten-year luck is even, the line states the app's rule that this year's own energy then sets the year's flow, so it is firm.
labels.why.rule.fixed: This kind of text has a set certainty instead of counting bases: it is always said as a tendency.
labels.why.rule.invest: How the flow is counted: money luck = 50 + wealth energy × 12 + ease of mind × 8. For a single day, the month's wealth energy × 4 is added. Either way it's kept between 0 and 100. Wealth energy +1 or more, ease of mind 0 or more and money luck 70 or more make a relaxed flow. Wealth energy −1 or less, ease of mind 0 or less and money luck 30 or less make a quiet flow. Anything else is an even flow.
labels.why.rule.match: How match certainty is set: each kind of paragraph has a set certainty. Kinds picked from a single basis (the two day stems, the two day branches, the year's flow or the year's branch) are tendencies. Only kinds picked when different bases point the same way, such as a day-stem clash together with a day-branch clash, are firm. “Something to try” and “Something to try together” are suggestions.

personality.summary.gap: Your chart points to an upright, dependable nature. You usually step forward first to open the way, and you watch over the people around you with a generous heart.
personality.detail.gap: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you have a strong drive to open new paths, so you're often the first to jump into what no one has touched yet. Your words and actions are straight, and you keep your word, so people trust you and lean on you. When someone close to you is in trouble, you stand in front of them, and you let small mistakes go with a generous heart. Once you feel you're right, though, you dig in your heels, and other views reach you late. When you feel most certain, ask someone else what they think once more before you decide.
personality.summary.eul: Your chart points to a gentle, flexible nature. You usually get along well with people wherever you are, and you have a persistence that doesn't give way easily.
personality.detail.eul: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you're good at finding your way when things change, so you often settle in fast even in unfamiliar places. Your words and manner are kind, and you smoothly bridge the gap between people who feel awkward with each other. You come across as gentle, but you don't break easily, so you hold out to the end on things that take a long time. Since you fit in so well wherever you are, when a group is deciding something, say at least one thing you want, and say it first.
personality.summary.byeong: Your chart points to a bright, optimistic nature. You're full of passion, you don't hide what you feel, and you're usually glad to share what you have.
personality.detail.byeong: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you start things with fiery momentum, so when you begin something new you often get the people around you going too. You look for the bright side first even in hard times, and you say what you think, so people don't have to guess what's on your mind. When something good comes your way, you share it with the people around you instead of keeping it to yourself. When your momentum builds, though, you put your own view first, and other people's voices get drowned out. When you pick up speed, look back now and then to see whether the people with you are keeping up.
personality.summary.jeong: Your chart points to a gentle, warm nature. You usually take thoughtful care of the people around you, and you truly want to be a source of strength for them.
personality.detail.jeong: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, your words and ways are gentle, so even shy people often relax once they're near you. You notice what people need before they say it and take care of it, so you're a steady source of strength for those close to you. Your feelings rise and fall, though, and when your spirits sink, the energy you put into caring for others shrinks with them. Once a week, set aside time just to look after your own feelings, with no one else to take care of.
personality.summary.mu: Your chart points to a grounded, steady nature. You don't say much, but you keep to your principles and often give the people around you something solid to lean on.
personality.detail.mu: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you have a strength that doesn't shake easily, so when things get hectic around you, you're usually the one who keeps things steady. Once you take something on, you carry it through by your principles, without letting up, so people trust you with things. When someone close to you is having a hard time, you quietly stay by their side. You rarely put your inner thoughts into words, though, so even people close to you are left guessing what you think. With people you trust, when something weighs on you, share how you feel before you share your conclusion.
personality.summary.gi: Your chart points to a kind, caring nature. You have a wide range of skills, and you often help the people around you grow.
personality.detail.gi: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you add a skill to whatever you touch, so you typically do the work of several people on your own. You care deeply about looking after people and helping them grow, so when someone fumbles with something new, you guide them step by step. When it's time to decide, though, you doubt your own judgment, and the decision keeps getting pushed back. When you hesitate, write down the date you'll decide by, and when that date comes, go with your own judgment.
personality.summary.gyeong: Your chart points to a resolute, loyal nature. You don't waver over what you believe is right, and you usually stand firmly by the people you care about.
personality.detail.gyeong: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you have a toughness that doesn't bend, so you often hold your ground instead of backing down when things get hard. You treasure the bonds you've made, and you clearly choose the side you believe is right. When someone you care about is in trouble, you rush to help before they even ask. Use that toughness to protect the people around you rather than to get the better of someone.
personality.summary.sin: Your chart points to a meticulous, quick-witted nature. You refine whatever you take on with care, and you often find new ways forward with original ideas.
personality.detail.sin: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you have a knack for polishing even the small details, so whatever passes through your hands generally comes out a step better. You think fast and speak with wit, so you draw people's attention when they gather. You care a lot about how others see you and about saving face, though, so your satisfaction rises and falls with other people's opinions. When you finish something, write down one thing that went well by your own standard before you hear anyone else's opinion.
personality.summary.im: Your chart points to a reflective, wise nature. You aim high, and you usually move with energy toward wider horizons.
personality.detail.im: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you see the wide view and think ahead, so while others look at what's right in front of them, you're often already looking at what comes next. You aren't afraid to dive into something new, and you move toward your goals with real force. When you have several things going at once, settle the order before you dive in. Each time you get past a hard stretch, look back over the road you've traveled, then choose your next direction.
personality.summary.gye: Your chart points to an imaginative nature and a flexible mind. Your interests usually branch out in many directions, and you know how to adapt to whatever each moment calls for.
personality.detail.gye: Going by your day stem, the sign that stands for you, you have a strong power to picture things in your mind, so you often come up with things others haven't thought of. Your interests are wide, so you move freely between fields and shift your thinking to fit the situation. Your interest moves on quickly, though, so you jump to the next thing before what you started is finished. Pick one thing you feel drawn to and keep at it for three months, and in the meantime, put new interests on a list and leave them there.
unit.lean.bigeop.core: Across your whole chart, the peer group, the energy of self and peers, is the largest, so a lot of your strength usually goes into acting on your own standards and will. That strength grows firmer when like-minded peers are by your side.
unit.lean.bigeop.scene: For example, even when a group is choosing, you often go with what you're convinced of over what most people picked.
unit.lean.bigeop.basis: Modern guides broadly agree that the peer group, the energy that matches your own, stands for self, will and peers.
unit.lean.siksang.core: Across your whole chart, the expression group, the energy of expression and skill, is the largest, so a lot of your strength usually goes into putting your ideas and skills out into the world and making things.
unit.lean.siksang.scene: For example, an idea that comes to you gets clearer mostly when you say it out loud or make something from it, not when you keep it in your head.
unit.lean.siksang.basis: Modern guides broadly agree that the expression group, the energy you give out, stands for expression, skill and making things.
unit.lean.jaeseong.core: Across your whole chart, the wealth group, the energy of wealth and results, is the largest, so a lot of your strength usually goes into producing tangible results and looking after them. You're also quick to go over what you've achieved and keep it in good order.
unit.lean.jaeseong.scene: For example, you typically feel more rewarded checking what's actually left once something is done than drawing up the plan.
unit.lean.jaeseong.basis: Modern guides broadly agree that the wealth group, the energy you manage, stands for wealth, results and looking after resources.
unit.lean.gwanseong.core: Across your whole chart, the duty group, the energy of duty and order, is the largest, so a lot of your strength usually goes into keeping to your roles and standards. You don't take your part in a group or an organization lightly.
unit.lean.gwanseong.scene: For example, when circumstances change, you generally keep what you promised first and only then think about what's next.
unit.lean.gwanseong.basis: Modern guides broadly agree that the duty group, the energy that steadies you, stands for duty, order and organizations.
unit.lean.inseong.core: Across your whole chart, the learning group, the energy of learning and support, is the largest, so a lot of your strength usually goes into learning, thinking things through and backing others up.
unit.lean.inseong.scene: For example, when you face something new, you're often more at ease once you've looked into it and understood it before you move.
unit.lean.inseong.basis: Modern guides broadly agree that the learning group, the energy that feeds you, stands for learning, support and care.
unit.scene.bigyeon.core: The sign of your birth month is Bigyeon, the energy of peers and equals, so your strength shows when you have room to do things your own way. When you've made the call yourself, you take responsibility for how it turns out.
unit.scene.bigyeon.scene: For example, when you're learning something new, your motivation lasts longer if you follow a plan you made yourself from start to finish rather than an order someone else set.
unit.scene.bigyeon.caution: When you have to set your own way aside or get compared with others, your heart grows heavy and you feel like dropping even what you were doing. When a comparison comes up, measure yourself against where you were three months ago instead of against other people.
unit.scene.bigyeon.suggestion: When opinions split, first sort out the one thing you must keep from the things you'll give way on.
unit.scene.bigyeon.basis: Modern guides broadly read Bigyeon, the energy that matches your own, as will, equality and independence.
unit.scene.geopjae.core: The sign of your birth month is Geopjae, the energy of rivalry and drive, so your strength shows when the goal is clear and you need to move fast. Having someone to compete with speeds you up even more.
unit.scene.geopjae.scene: For example, when people are competing, your focus sharpens as things near the end, and you move a step ahead of the rest.
unit.scene.geopjae.caution: When you keep being measured against others, impatience sets in and you rush even the decisions that need weighing. When you feel the urge to decide in a hurry, run it by one person you trust before you settle it.
unit.scene.geopjae.suggestion: When things pile up, sort out ahead of time what to do fast and what to look over slowly.
unit.scene.geopjae.basis: Modern guides broadly read Geopjae as competition, drive and impulse.
unit.scene.siksin.core: The sign of your birth month is Siksin, the energy of enjoyment and craft, so your strength shows when you feel unhurried and there's no need to rush. The more you enjoy what you're doing, the more your skill comes alive.
unit.scene.siksin.scene: For example, when you take up a hobby and enjoy it slowly without racing the clock, your skill grows noticeably.
unit.scene.siksin.caution: When things pile on without a break, the enjoyment goes first, and then your skill dulls too. When things get hectic, do at least one task in a way you enjoy.
unit.scene.siksin.suggestion: When you're busy, don't leave rest to whatever time is left over; give it its own slot in your schedule.
unit.scene.siksin.basis: Modern guides broadly read Siksin as enjoyment, skill and an easygoing pace.
unit.scene.sanggwan.core: The sign of your birth month is Sanggwan, the energy of wit and bold expression, so your strength shows when you can speak your mind freely and your ideas are taken up. You spot what needs fixing in familiar ways before anyone else does.
unit.scene.sanggwan.scene: For example, when you're in a group where any idea is welcome, you're the first to point out what others missed.
unit.scene.sanggwan.caution: When you have to follow set rules with no room for questions, frustration builds, and complaints about the rules themselves come out first. When a rule feels stifling, first ask why it was made.
unit.scene.sanggwan.suggestion: When you have a point to make, write it down before you bring it up.
unit.scene.sanggwan.basis: Modern guides broadly read Sanggwan as talent, self-expression and pushing back against rules.
unit.scene.pyeonjae.core: The sign of your birth month is Pyeonjae, the energy of opportunity and wide connections, so your strength shows when you're in lively settings where new people and tasks keep coming and going. At those times, your eye for the chances that open up between people gets sharper too.
unit.scene.pyeonjae.scene: For example, when you have to meet many people and switch between tasks in a single day, you gain energy instead of wearing out.
unit.scene.pyeonjae.caution: When long stretches of the same routine go on, boredom builds, and you let go of what you were doing to look at something new before it's finished. When you feel like starting something new, first set a date to wrap up what you're already doing.
unit.scene.pyeonjae.suggestion: Add a small goal or a new approach, one at a time, even to routine tasks.
unit.scene.pyeonjae.basis: Modern guides broadly read Pyeonjae as a feel for business and for connecting with people.
unit.scene.jeongjae.core: The sign of your birth month is Jeongjae, the energy of steady, practical wealth, so your strength shows when what needs doing, and in what order, is clearly set. That's when your diligence in covering every part of a task shines.
unit.scene.jeongjae.scene: For example, when you're learning something new, you feel settled and keep going longer if you set a daily amount and finish it piece by piece.
unit.scene.jeongjae.caution: When plans change suddenly or small worries pile up, you weigh each one so closely that you have no energy left for the big decisions. Write small worries down in one place and go over them together at a set time.
unit.scene.jeongjae.suggestion: When plans change, settle the one thing you'll keep first and adjust the rest slowly.
unit.scene.jeongjae.basis: Modern guides broadly read Jeongjae as consistency, practicality and diligence.
unit.scene.pyeongwan.core: The sign of your birth month is Pyeongwan, the energy of pressure and resolve, so your strength shows when you take on what others hesitate over and have to set the direction. The heavier the pressure, the clearer your resolve becomes.
unit.scene.pyeongwan.scene: For example, when a plan you made with others gets tangled, you step up first and sort out who does what.
unit.scene.pyeongwan.caution: When pressure keeps coming without a break, your energy wears down fast and your words turn harsh. When the pressure drags on, don't hold out alone; hand one of your loads to someone else.
unit.scene.pyeongwan.suggestion: After you get through something big, deliberately set aside time to rest.
unit.scene.pyeongwan.basis: Modern guides broadly read Pyeongwan as pressure, challenge and decisiveness.
unit.scene.jeonggwan.core: The sign of your birth month is Jeonggwan, the energy of order and responsibility, so your strength shows when roles and procedures are clear. Within rules that were set fairly, you act properly and dependably.
unit.scene.jeonggwan.scene: For example, when you're learning something and the steps and standards are clearly laid out, you work through them carefully, leaving no gaps.
unit.scene.jeonggwan.caution: When promises keep changing or standards are fuzzy, you grow uneasy and put off even small decisions while watching how others react. When you want to put a decision off, weigh only what's fairest and decide by that.
unit.scene.jeonggwan.suggestion: When the standards are unclear, set your own before you get moving.
unit.scene.jeonggwan.basis: Modern guides broadly read Jeonggwan as order, responsibility and good standing.
unit.scene.pyeonin.core: The sign of your birth month is Pyeonin, the energy of original thinking and intuition, so your strength shows when an answer of your own is needed rather than one handed to you. You sense the direction first and work out the reasons later.
unit.scene.pyeonin.scene: For example, when a question comes up in your studies that others pass by, you hold on to it and think it through until an unexpected answer comes to you.
unit.scene.pyeonin.caution: When you turn things over on your own, one doubt leads to the next, and you miss the moment to share your thoughts. When the doubts keep coming, stop turning them over, pick just one thing that bothers you and check the facts on it.
unit.scene.pyeonin.suggestion: Once your thoughts are in order, tell someone close to you first.
unit.scene.pyeonin.basis: Modern guides read Pyeonin as original thinking and time alone, and also link it to overthinking.
unit.scene.jeongin.core: The sign of your birth month is Jeongin, the energy of learning and support, so your strength shows when you can learn calmly among people you trust. With someone backing you up nearby, your deep, careful judgment comes alive too.
unit.scene.jeongin.scene: For example, if someone you can ask freely is nearby, you quickly make even unfamiliar things your own.
unit.scene.jeongin.caution: When someone to lean on is close by, you keep handing your decisions to others, and you get fewer chances to use your own judgment. Before you ask anyone, write down your own answer in a line first.
unit.scene.jeongin.suggestion: When there's something new to learn, block out plenty of time in your schedule to take it in.
unit.scene.jeongin.basis: Modern guides broadly read Jeongin as learning, care and relying on others.

bridge.outgoing_inward: Two strands in your chart split how you show up with people. When you're among people you know well, you start the conversations and set the mood; when you're with strangers, you step back and watch first.
bridge.steady_change: Two strands in your chart split how you take on change. When the familiar way still works, you keep at it steadily; when the ground shifts, you're among the first to look for a new way.
bridge.active_rest: Two strands in your chart call for action and rest in turn. When the task is clear, you keep moving without a break; once it's done, you need quiet time on your own to recharge before you go again.
bridge.speed_careful: Two strands in your chart set your pace by the size of the decision. When a choice is small and easy to undo, you make it on the spot; when it's big and hard to take back, you weigh it for a long time first.
bridge.express_listen: Two strands in your chart divide the times you speak from the times you listen. When you're with people you click with, you speak your mind freely; when opinions split, you listen all the way through first.
bridge.spend_save: Two strands in your chart split your spending by what the money is for. When it goes to people and experiences, you spend freely; when it's something just for yourself, you hold back and think it over.
bridge.together_alone: Two strands in your chart split what you share from what you keep in your own hands. When people share your goal, you gladly work hand in hand; when it comes to how the work gets done, you decide that yourself.

unit.stage.jangsaeng.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at jangsaeng (長生). The stage is often likened to the moment of birth in a person's life.
unit.stage.jangsaeng.strength: When you're learning something or trying it for the first time, curiosity usually comes before worry. Classical texts call this seat the hall of learning (學堂) and see a knack for picking up new things in it too.
unit.stage.jangsaeng.caution: When you start something, you typically draw up a big first plan. Then the first few steps take a lot out of you. Keep the first step small when you set out.
unit.stage.jangsaeng.suggestion: When you reach the first goal of something new, set the next goal that same day.
unit.stage.mogyok.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at mogyok (沐浴). The stage is often likened to a sprout washing off its old husk.
unit.stage.mogyok.strength: When long-running work stalls, you generally look at it with fresh eyes and clear out what's gone stale.
unit.stage.mogyok.caution: When a new method catches your eye, you're inclined to switch before your current one has settled. Then what you've built up scatters. Before you switch, keep the current one going for a full season.
unit.stage.mogyok.suggestion: Once a year, pick one habit to drop and one to take up, both at the same time.
unit.stage.gwandae.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at gwandae (冠帶). The stage is often likened to coming of age in a person's life, when the cap and sash are put on.
unit.stage.gwandae.strength: When you take on a new place or role, you usually start by building up the methods and manner it calls for, one piece at a time.
unit.stage.gwandae.caution: When you want to get something just right, you generally spend your energy on format and procedure first. Then there's less time left to build real skill. Before you polish the format, decide on one thing to learn first.
unit.stage.gwandae.suggestion: Write down, in one line, the next step for whatever you're shaping right now, and check on it every season.
unit.stage.geollok.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at geollok (建祿). The stage is often likened to the point in a person's life when they've grown strong and are ready to take office.
unit.stage.geollok.strength: When a role is given to you, you usually take charge of your part and run it. Classical texts liken this seat to the office of letters (詞館) and see a way with words in it too.
unit.stage.geollok.caution: Once something is in your hands, you typically see to every part of it yourself, start to finish. Then, even when it gets heavy, you miss the chance to ask for help. Before you begin, set one date midway to go over progress with the people involved.
unit.stage.geollok.suggestion: Write up how you work on a single page and share it with the people you work with.
unit.stage.jewang.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at jewang (帝旺). The stage is often likened to the prime of a person's life, when vigor is at its height.
unit.stage.jewang.strength: When a weighty task is handed to you, you usually steady yourself and rise to the occasion.
unit.stage.jewang.caution: When something important is at stake, you generally put everything else on hold. Then, once you're past the hardest part, the backlog lands on you all at once. Even in the middle of a big push, clear one small task every day.
unit.stage.jewang.suggestion: When you have strength to spare, pick one big goal and pour it all into that.
unit.stage.soe.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at soe (衰). The stage is often likened to the first turn energy takes after its peak.
unit.stage.soe.strength: Even in work whose heyday has passed, you usually pick out what's still useful and put it to new use.
unit.stage.soe.caution: Once you spot something to fix, you typically hold back even finished work. Then it misses the moment it was needed. Whenever you start on fixes, set the date you'll hand the work over.
unit.stage.soe.suggestion: Among the things you're doing now, pick one to cut back and one to refine further, and write them down.
unit.stage.byeong.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at the byeong stage, which is often likened to the point where energy, past its peak, grows calmer still.
unit.stage.byeong.strength: With things that aren't urgent, you usually go step by step at your own pace instead of rushing.
unit.stage.byeong.caution: When you have to match someone else's pace, you generally push your own work to the back. Then, as the deadline nears, it all piles up at once. When you take on fast-moving work, say up front when your part will be done.
unit.stage.byeong.suggestion: For anything that takes a long time, set a few midway goals that fit your stride.
unit.stage.sa.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at the sa stage, which is often likened to a still point once one cycle has run its full course.
unit.stage.sa.strength: When you finish something, you generally wrap it up cleanly, with nothing left hanging, before you move on.
unit.stage.sa.caution: Since you put finished work away so neatly, you typically don't go back to what you gained from it. Then you spend the same effort all over again next time. Before you put something away, gather anything reusable in one place.
unit.stage.sa.suggestion: When you start something new, first look through what you kept from similar work in the past.
unit.stage.myo.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at the myo stage, which is often likened to a storehouse where things are gathered and kept.
unit.stage.myo.strength: When you finish something, you generally gather up the material and experience it left you with and keep it for the long run.
unit.stage.myo.caution: As your store grows, you usually start losing track of what's where. Then, when you need something, it takes time to find. Label what you keep and list it all in one place.
unit.stage.myo.suggestion: Pick one thing from the material or experience you've stored up and put it to use within this season.
unit.stage.jeol.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at jeol (絕). The stage is often likened to the point where the old energy breaks off and the new is about to carry on.
unit.stage.jeol.strength: Once it's clear something doesn't fit, you generally let it go without lingering and get ready for what's next.
unit.stage.jeol.caution: When you end something, you typically make such a clean break that you also drop the parts worth carrying on. Then the ties and skills you built up scatter along with it. Before you wrap something up, pick one person or skill from it to carry forward.
unit.stage.jeol.suggestion: When you start something new, build one lesson from the last thing into your first plan.
unit.stage.tae.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at tae (胎). The stage is often likened to new energy gathering and taking form.
unit.stage.tae.strength: When your thoughts scatter in several directions, you usually pull them together into a single plan.
unit.stage.tae.caution: You generally work on a new plan alone until it feels complete. Then you get fewer chances to refine it through other people's eyes. As soon as the first line is down, show someone that line.
unit.stage.tae.suggestion: When a plan comes to you, write it down along with one first step you'll take this week.
unit.stage.yang.core: Seen through the twelve stages, the branch of the day you were born (your day branch) is at yang (養). This nurturing stage is often likened to the time before birth, when a person is being cared for and growing.
unit.stage.yang.strength: When you get help or teaching, you usually hold on to it and turn it into skill of your own.
unit.stage.yang.caution: With things that take a long time to grow, you typically wait for results and skip the check-ins along the way. Then, if the direction drifts, you notice late. For anything long-term, check the direction once every three months.
unit.stage.yang.suggestion: When you next get the chance to help someone, pass on the teaching you received, just as it was given to you.
unit.spirit.noble.core: With the Nobleman Star (cheoneul gwiin, 天乙貴人) in your chart, there's often someone beside you who helps when things get hard. Still, a single star doesn't decide how things turn out.
unit.spirit.noble.scene: For example, when you open up about something too hard to untangle alone, you typically get a lead from someone nearby.
unit.spirit.noble.suggestion: When you're stuck, first pin down exactly where, then ask one person you trust about just that part.
unit.spirit.literary.core: With the Academic Star (munchang gwiin, 文昌貴人) in your chart, your sharp mind usually shows when you read, write or study something in depth. A knack for explaining what you've learned to others in your own words comes with it.
unit.spirit.literary.scene: For example, when a pile of complex material lands in front of you, you're often the one who ends up picking out the key points and writing them up.
unit.spirit.literary.suggestion: Pick one field that interests you and read one book on it from cover to cover.
unit.spirit.travel.core: With the Traveling Horse (yeokma, 驛馬) in your chart, trips, work travel and changes of place often come into your life. Your energy picks up more when you're on the move than when you stay put for long.
unit.spirit.travel.scene: For example, while you're moving between unfamiliar places, ideas that didn't come to you at your desk usually fall into place.
unit.spirit.travel.suggestion: When a move or a long trip comes up, list what needs wrapping up before you leave.
unit.spirit.canopy.core: With the Canopy Star (hwagae, 華蓋) in your chart, when a field of study or a craft grabs you, you're inclined to go deep into it on your own. You reach places others rarely do and work what you find into real skill.
unit.spirit.canopy.scene: For example, when a question catches your interest, you often dig up material and practice on your own, with no one asking you to.
unit.spirit.canopy.suggestion: Make something small and finished out of what you've been digging into, and show it to at least one person.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.core: The branches of the year and month you were born form a clash (chung, 沖), so the ground you grew up on and your road out into the world point in different directions. That's why you usually carve out your own footing early on.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.scene: For example, when you choose a career or a way of living, you often follow a path you found yourself rather than the one taken for granted where you grew up.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.suggestion: From what you picked up growing up, choose one thing to take with you as you find your own footing.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.eased.core: The branches of the year and month you were born form a clash (chung, 沖) that pulls two ways, but another branch in your chart makes a pairing (hap, 合) with one of them and eases the strain. So even when you carve out your own footing, you keep your ties to the ground you grew up on.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.eased.scene: For example, when you choose a career, you're drawn away from the path that was familiar where you grew up, but once you've decided, you find a way to connect the two.
unit.pair.year_month.clash.eased.suggest: When the two sides pull apart, look first for a person or a way that can link them.
unit.pair.year_month.combine.core: The branches of the year and month you were born form a pairing (hap, 合), so the ground you grew up on and the role you take on in the world go hand in hand. What you learned early usually carries straight over into work and dealings with people, but when the two mesh too tightly, they can tie you to familiar patterns.
unit.pair.year_month.combine.scene: For example, the way of talking and working you picked up growing up often works just as well in new places.
unit.pair.year_month.combine.suggestion: When your familiar ways are working well, switch one thing to a new way anyway.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.core: The branches of the year and day you were born form a clash (chung, 沖). They sit apart, so the pull is mild, but you usually rely on what you've built yourself more than on what was handed down to you.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.scene: For example, when you hit a wall, you often think first of the skills and people you've gathered on your own, rather than looking for something to lean on.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.suggestion: Once a year, write down the skills and contacts you've built up on your own.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.eased.core: The branches of the year and day you were born form a clash (chung, 沖) from a distance, but another branch in your chart makes a pairing (hap, 合) with one of them and takes the edge off. So even when you rely on what you've built yourself, you don't drift away from the background you came from.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.eased.scene: For example, when you run things your own way, you take a different road from the one handed down, but when you get stuck, you find something useful in that background.
unit.pair.year_day.clash.eased.suggestio: Choose ahead of time one long-standing connection you'll go to for advice when you're stuck.
unit.lean.bigeop.firm.core: Across your whole chart, the peer group, the energy of self and peers, is the largest, and the sign of your birth month belongs to it too, so a lot of your strength goes into acting on your own standards and will. That strength grows firmer when like-minded peers are by your side.
unit.lean.siksang.firm.core: Across your whole chart, the expression group, the energy of expression and skill, is the largest, and the sign of your birth month belongs to it too, so a lot of your strength goes into putting your ideas and skills out into the world and making things.
unit.lean.jaeseong.firm.core: Across your whole chart, the wealth group, the energy of wealth and results, is the largest, and the sign of your birth month belongs to it too, so a lot of your strength goes into producing tangible results and looking after them. You're also quick to go over what you've achieved and keep it in good order.
unit.lean.gwanseong.firm.core: Across your whole chart, the duty group, the energy of duty and order, is the largest, and the sign of your birth month belongs to it too, so a lot of your strength goes into keeping to your roles and standards. You don't take your part in a group or an organization lightly.
unit.lean.inseong.firm.core: Across your whole chart, the learning group, the energy of learning and support, is the largest, and the sign of your birth month belongs to it too, so a lot of your strength goes into learning, thinking things through and backing others up.

love.draw.bigyeon.core: With Bigyeon, the energy of peers and equals, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually want an equal relationship where neither of you leads or follows, even with the person closest to you. You open up when you respect each other's work and time, and a relationship that ties you down too tightly feels stifling.
love.draw.bigyeon.scene: For example, even when you first grow close, the bond often deepens through doing things side by side, like working out together or sharing a hobby. Even after you become close, you love the friendly teasing and talk.
love.draw.bigyeon.strength: You treat the other person as an equal, so even when you disagree, you usually listen without putting their view down. Because you each respect the other's share, you sort out what doesn't fit calmly. Even together, you leave each other room of your own.
love.draw.bigyeon.caution: That said, since you do fine on your own, you often try to handle things alone even when you need help, without saying so. When something hard comes up, try asking the other person for even one small thing.
love.draw.geopjae.core: With Geopjae, the energy of rivalry and drive, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually make the first move toward someone you're drawn to. You get closer by trying things out rather than holding back. Instead of hiding your feelings for long, you bring them out and watch how the other person responds.
love.draw.geopjae.scene: For example, when you're drawn to someone, you often set up the plan yourself instead of waiting for a message, even deciding where to meet and what to do. Once you feel a connection, the relationship usually picks up speed fast.
love.draw.geopjae.strength: You have the courage not to hesitate, so when a relationship gets stuck, you usually speak up first and get things moving again. When someone close is in trouble, you step in as if it were your own problem. You're the one who reaches out first to someone who hesitates.
love.draw.geopjae.caution: That said, your feelings run ahead and you pick up speed, so you often push a relationship forward before the other person is ready. When you suggest the next step, don't settle the answer in advance; hear their thoughts first.
love.draw.siksin.core: With Siksin, the energy of enjoyment and craft, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually want the simple joy of eating, laughing and resting together in a close relationship. You open up as easy time together adds up. Your heart goes more to someone who makes fun things by hand and shares them.
love.draw.siksin.scene: For example, finding a good place to eat together or sharing food at home often turns into a date, and closeness grows out of those small moments. Even with no special plan, you enjoy walking around the neighborhood or cooking together.
love.draw.siksin.strength: You have an ease that helps people unwind, so even on days when someone close is worn out, you usually make room for them to rest. You don't let small pleasures slip by; you share them. You can lighten even a heavy mood.
love.draw.siksin.caution: That said, to protect the comfort you have, you often put off the talks that would move the relationship a step forward. When you start wondering about the next step, ask about it briefly yourself.
love.draw.sanggwan.core: With Sanggwan, the energy of wit and bold expression, in the branch of the day you were born, you're usually drawn to people you can trade quick wit with. You grow close through honest back-and-forth talk. You're drawn more to someone who suggests changing set ways together.
love.draw.sanggwan.scene: For example, if jokes and quick replies fly back and forth, you get close fast even at a first meeting, and talks with someone you click with often run late into the night. You catch what someone means quickly and answer with wit.
love.draw.sanggwan.strength: You have the power to put feelings into words, so you usually say thanks and hurt feelings as they come instead of hiding them. Because you don't hide them, misunderstandings have little room to pile up. Your love of good conversation keeps the relationship lively.
love.draw.sanggwan.caution: That said, because you chase what's new and fun, you often feel bored once a relationship gets familiar. Even in a familiar relationship, pick one new thing to try together.
love.draw.pyeonjae.core: With Pyeonjae, the energy of opportunity and wide connections, in the branch of the day you were born, you meet people widely and usually grow close naturally to those you click with. You want a relationship that goes to new places together. Your feelings grow in relationships that move and take things on together, not ones that stay in one place.
love.draw.pyeonjae.scene: For example, you get close to someone you met in a group after hanging out several times, or the bond often deepens on trips and at shows together. Your circle of friends and your love life sometimes blend naturally.
love.draw.pyeonjae.strength: You have a generosity that shares freely, so you usually give your time and heart freely to the people close to you. You're someone who keeps widening the experiences you share. You go looking for joys the other person hadn't found yet.
love.draw.pyeonjae.caution: That said, because your attention spreads wide, settling deeply on one person often comes late. When there's someone you want to get closer to, create one thing you do only with them.
love.draw.jeongjae.core: With Jeongjae, the energy of steady, practical wealth, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually want a relationship of steady care rather than a flashy start. Watching small promises being kept brings you closer. You grow close slowly, at the pace trust builds, rather than on excitement.
love.draw.jeongjae.scene: For example, you often remember something the other person said in passing and take care of what they need, and you plan your dates and what to do ahead of time. You feel at ease once the money and time you'll spend together are settled in advance.
love.draw.jeongjae.strength: Your care is steady rather than wordy, so you usually look after the daily life of the people close to you thoroughly. You calmly line up the plans and household numbers you'll share. When someone close is in a tight spot, you look for a practical way out first.
love.draw.jeongjae.caution: That said, because you weigh plans and practicality first, showing your feelings falls behind and the relationship often turns dry. Now and then, mix in something unplanned, like a small surprise gift or message.
love.draw.pyeongwan.core: With Pyeongwan, the energy of pressure and resolve, in the branch of the day you were born, once your mind is made up you usually go in deep without hesitating. You're drawn to a solid bond where you protect each other. You want something serious, not a light back-and-forth.
love.draw.pyeongwan.scene: For example, even if you say little at first, the bond often deepens all at once after you get through one hard thing together. You make up your mind by watching how the other person handles difficulty.
love.draw.pyeongwan.strength: You have the resolve to step forward in hard times, so when something big happens in a close relationship, you usually hold steady. You look after the person you've chosen to protect to the end. You don't step back even one pace in the face of difficulty.
love.draw.pyeongwan.caution: That said, your urge to protect is strong, so you often try to decide even the other person's matters for them. Sort out what to help with and what to watch, and leave the watching part alone while you wait.
love.draw.jeonggwan.core: With Jeonggwan, the energy of order and responsibility, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually want a relationship where you can trust each other and the promises are clear. You get closer one step at a time, in order. Once the relationship has a name and clear promises, you give your heart fully.
love.draw.jeonggwan.scene: For example, you don't show your feelings easily until the relationship is clear, and you often come to see someone in a new light when they keep the promises they made. You're careful at first, but once trust forms, you line up much of your daily life together.
love.draw.jeonggwan.strength: You have a sense of responsibility others can rely on, so in a relationship you've committed to, you usually keep your share to the end. You bring order and stability to the daily life of the people close to you. You don't take shared promises lightly.
love.draw.jeonggwan.caution: That said, since you think first about what has to be kept, showing your feelings often comes late. Even before the relationship is clear, say kind feelings out loud as they come.
love.draw.pyeonin.core: With Pyeonin, the energy of original thinking and intuition, in the branch of the day you were born, you're usually drawn to people who appreciate your unusual way of thinking. You open up when your time alone is respected. You're at ease in a relationship that accepts each person's own world, more than one where you do everything together.
love.draw.pyeonin.scene: For example, you get close fast to someone who listens with interest when you talk about a niche interest, and your feelings usually stay the same even through long stretches apart. When you're together, you get lost in talk only the two of you share.
love.draw.pyeonin.strength: You have an understanding that sees people with different eyes, so you usually read deeply into feelings that don't show on the surface. You express your feelings in ways that aren't predictable. You pick up on a worry before the other person puts it into words.
love.draw.pyeonin.caution: That said, because you're drawn to the unusual, you often find an ordinary, steady routine boring. Even in a familiar routine, set up one small habit only the two of you share and keep it going.
love.draw.jeongin.core: With Jeongin, the energy of learning and support, in the branch of the day you were born, you usually want a relationship you can lean on with an easy heart. You grow close in the warmth of caring for and accepting each other. Your heart stays long with someone you can lean on and learn from.
love.draw.jeongin.scene: For example, your heart often leans toward someone who listens on a hard day, and once you're close, you even look after their meals and rest. You naturally stay by someone's side when they're sick or worn out.
love.draw.jeongin.strength: You have a warm embrace that takes people in, so you usually forgive the people close to you when they slip up. You're someone who makes a place where others can rest. You accept even their clumsy sides as they are.
love.draw.jeongin.caution: That said, when the urge to lean grows, you hand over even the decisions, and one side often ends up carrying more. On days you want to lean, say so in words first.
